content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_9/projects/event-gated-adaptive-horizon/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing: Diagnostic Analysis of Temporal Abstraction in World-Model RL\\n\\n## Title Candidates\\n\\n1. **\\\"Why Temporal Abstraction Fails in DreamerV3: A Diagnostic Analysis of Variable-Rate Imagination\\\"**\\n2. ~~**\\\"The Delusional Critic Problem in DreamerV3's Variable-Rate Imagination\\\"**~~ (deprecated — \\\"delusional critic\\\" conflicts with Lu et al. 2018)\\n3. **\\\"Diagnosing Value Overestimation from Temporal Abstraction in DreamerV3\\\"** ← preferred after D037 terminology decision\\n4. **\\\"Conditioning-Induced Value Overestimation in Variable-Rate World-Model Imagination\\\"**\\n\\n**⚠️ D037 术语决定**: \\\"delusional critic\\\" → **\\\"conditioning-induced value overestimation\\\"** (简称 CIVO)。Lu et al. 2018 的 delusional bias 指 policy-class constraints 导致不可实现的 Q 值，本文机制是 model imprecision + learned conditioning amplification，概念不同。Dream 模拟三档审稿一致指出术语误导。全文替换：\\\"delusional critic\\\" → \\\"conditioning-induced value overestimation\\\"，可 cite Lu et al. 2018 as analogy but must explicitly differentiate。\\n\\n**⚠️ D037 TAWM 对比（关键 novelty 升级）**: TAWM (Nhu et al., ICML 2025) 在 TD-MPC2 (MPC setting) 中成功使用 dt-conditioning。本文发现 dt-conditioning 在 imagination-based actor-critic 中失败 → **novelty 从 \\\"known failure class 的 specific instance\\\" 升级为 \\\"dt-conditioning succeeds in MPC but fails in imagination — here's the architecture-specific vulnerability\\\"**。TAWM 是强化 novelty 的最关键参考文献。\\n\\n## Venue\\n\\n**CoRL 2026** — Deadline: 2026-05-29\\n\\n## Narrative Positioning\\n\\nThis is a **diagnostic analysis paper**, not a method paper. We do not propose a new algorithm. Instead, we provide a systematic, controlled investigation answering: *Why does temporal abstraction fail in world-model RL?*\\n\\nThe contribution is a **strongly supported causal chain** from mechanism to failure mode, backed by a factorial experiment design that isolates each factor, plus a **practical mitigation guideline** (restrict imagination to dt=1 during multi-dt training → 95% baseline recovery). Diagnostic papers are valued when they (a) address a widely-attempted but poorly-understood failure, (b) provide actionable insight for future method design, and (c) are methodologically rigorous.\\n\\nWe scope all claims to **DreamerV3 and its RSSM world model**. Generalizability to other latent-dynamics architectures is discussed but not claimed.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Core Claims\\n\\n### C1: Variable-rate imagination in DreamerV3 consistently degrades performance\\n\\nTemporal abstraction via variable dt—whether learned or fixed—degrades asymptotic performance relative to the dt=1 baseline across all tested configurations.\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| Baseline stability | exp_001_baseline (dt=1) | Stable convergence ~950 eval return |\\n| Fixed dt=2 collapse | exp_006_fixed_dt2 (dt=2, subsample ON, H=15) | Peak 485@35K → collapse to ~135@65K |\\n| Fixed dt=4 severe degradation | exp_007_fixed_dt4 (dt=4) | Peak 176.9@25K, 144.4@45K (33% of baseline@45K=443) |\\n| Learned gate collapse | exp_005 (learned gate) | Peak 541@55K → 99@145K |\\n\\n**Strength**: Strong. Three independent dt>1 configurations all show degradation. No positive result exists for variable-rate imagination in our setup.\\n\\n### C2: Trained dt_embedding reliably triggers pathological value overestimation (>1.5x), creating high collapse risk\\n\\n**D032 update: nve>1.5x threshold has perfect separating power (4/4); collapse itself is stochastic.**\\n\\nThe trained dt_embedding reliably induces pathological value overestimation (normalized v/e >1.5x baseline) across all tested seeds, but whether this overestimation progresses to catastrophic performance collapse is stochastic:\\n\\n- **WITH trained dt_emb**: 2/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x at 35K+ (008d seed 1: sustained 1.71x@35K→2.09x@45K→4.12x@55K → collapse; 009b seed 2: 1.62x@45K → self-correction to 0.38x@105K)\\n- **WITHOUT dt_emb (008f)**: 0/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x at 35K+ (seed 1 peak 1.02x@25K; seed 2 peak 1.26x@25K)\\n- **1.5x threshold (35K+)**: 4/4 perfect classification — reliable diagnostic marker separating trained vs untrained dt_emb\\n\\n**⚠️ 时间限定**: nve>1.5x 诊断适用于 **35K+ steps**（此时 baseline v/e 已充分收敛至 >0.24，比率稳定可靠）。25K 处 baseline v/e 仅 0.087，微小绝对差异可被放大为大比率（如 009b@25K nve=2.05x 和 008e_v3@25K nve=1.93x 均为 false positive）。论文中报告 threshold 时必须标注此限定。\\n\\n**Sustained vs transient overestimation**: The key difference between collapse (008d seed 1) and self-correction (009b seed 2) is the **temporal persistence** of nve>1.5x. Seed 1 maintained nve>1.5x across 3 consecutive checkpoints at 35K+ (1.71x@35K→2.09x@45K→4.12x@55K, accelerating), locking the positive feedback loop; seed 2 exceeded 1.5x at 45K (1.62x) but dropped to 1.41x@55K and continued declining, allowing self-correction. This suggests a \\\"point of no return\\\" where sustained overestimation becomes irreversible, with early training stochasticity (initialization, data sampling order) determining which path is taken (cf. Henderson et al. 2018, Bjorck et al. 2022, Qiao et al. 2023).\\n\\nThe trained dt_embedding enables precise dt prediction in imagination, but RSSM state prediction quality at dt>1 is insufficient to support this precision. The result is conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO) that drives actor learning toward incorrect policies. Without dt_embedding conditioning, the overestimation feedback loop is blocked entirely (nve never exceeds 1.5x).\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| Untrained dt_emb, no collapse | exp_008c (dt=2, subsample OFF, untrained dt_emb, H=8) | eval plateau ~242@55K; v/e: @35K=21.8% (0.90x) → @55K=29.1% (0.72x) → @65K=32.8% (0.58x) (declining normalized v/e, ~7x slower than trained) |\\n| Trained dt_emb, collapse | exp_008d (dt=2, subsample ON, trained dt_emb, H=8) | eval declining 167→146→141 @25K→35K→45K; v/e: @25K=15.5% (1.78x) → @35K=41.2% (1.71x) → @45K=69.3% (2.09x) (accelerating overestimation) |\\n| Both trained dt_emb → accelerating v/e | exp_006 (H=15) vs exp_008d (H=8) | 006: v/e @35K=31.1% (1.29x)→@45K=53.3% (1.61x)→@55K=93.3% (2.31x); 008d: v/e @35K=41.2% (1.71x)→@45K=69.3% (2.09x) — both show accelerating normalized v/e leading to collapse |\\n| Baseline v/e calibration (overshoot reference) | exp_001_baseline | v/e@35K=24.1%, @45K=33.1%, @55K=40.4%. Overshoot ratio: 008d@35K=1.7x, @45K=2.1x; 006@45K=1.6x, @55K=2.3x (all >1.5x = pathological) |\\n| **D032: Trained dt_emb seed 2 — pathological but self-correcting** | exp_009b (008d config, seed 2) | eval 39→141→164→141→172→209→197→236→279→268@105K (**no collapse**, rising). nve: **2.05x@25K**→1.24x→**1.62x@45K**→1.41x→0.94x→0.66x→0.51x→0.43x→**0.38x@105K**. Transient nve>1.5x with self-correction. Value peaked 110.9@65K → self-corrected to 67.3@105K while eval improved. |\\n| **1.5x threshold separating power** | 008d+009b vs 008f+009c | WITH trained dt_emb: 2/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x (008d peak 2.09x sustained, 009b peak 2.05x transient). WITHOUT dt_emb: 0/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x (008f peak 1.02x, 009c peak 1.26x). **4/4 perfect classification.** |\\n| **Causal control: dt_embed_dim=0 (direction confirmed, seed-dependent)** | exp_008f seed 1 + exp_009c seed 2 | **Seed 1**: eval 197→207→194→173→503@105K (zigzag recovery); nve 1.02x→0.73x→0.83x→0.97x→0.30x. **Seed 2**: eval 169→211→239→359→227→191→148@105K (decline after 75K); nve 1.26x→0.79x→0.72x→0.33x→0.60x→0.90x→1.14x. Both vs 008d@45K nve=2.09x: onset delayed 60K+ steps, severity reduced ~2x. **009c extending to 200K to observe if nve crosses 1.5x.** |\\n| **SGS (reward detach) 不阻断 CIVO** | exp_016e (reward_dt_emb_detach=True, subsample ON, H=8, seed 1) | Peak eval 326.7@75K → collapse 31.7@95K, NVE=10.42x. SGS delays onset ~50K steps (008d@45K vs 016e@95K) and raises peak 2x (327 vs 167), but collapse is more severe (NVE 10.42x vs 4.12x). **Reward gradient pathway is a contributing factor (explains delay) but not the sole root cause** — CIVO operates at representation level through world model training. |\\n| RSSM fidelity analysis | baseline / 008d / 008f | See RSSM Fidelity Table below |\\n\\n**⚠️ 008f 定位：因果控制实验，非推荐方案。** 008f 去掉 dt_embedding 后 reward_MAE=0.747（baseline 的 75x），reward head 无法区分 dt=1/dt=2（reward gap 仅 1.01x vs 008d 的 2.78x）。**D030 更新**：008f seed 2 (009c) 在 105K 达到 nve=1.14x（borderline），seed 1 为 0.30x——protection 不 robust。但 008f 两个 seed 的 v/e 增长速度均显著慢于 008d（008d@45K=2.09x vs 008f seed 2@105K=1.14x），确认 dt_embedding 是 primary amplifier。**C2 因果方向成立，但 \\\"eliminates\\\" 改为 \\\"significantly delays and reduces\\\"。推荐方案仍是 008e_v3（C6）**。\\n\\n**RSSM Fidelity Table（论文中必须同时报告绝对误差和比率）：**\\n\\n| Model | dt1 obs_MSE | dt2 obs_MSE | obs gap | dt1 reward_MAE | dt2 reward_MAE | reward gap |\\n|-------|------------|------------|---------|---------------|---------------|------------|\\n| baseline (exp_001) | 13.49 | 27.50 | **2.04x** | 0.0102 | 0.0159 | 1.56x |\\n| 008d (trained dt_emb, collapsed) | 41.31 | 53.67 | **1.30x** | 0.0568 | 0.1579 | **2.78x** |\\n| 008f (no dt_emb, stable) | 8.01 | 22.04 | **2.75x** | 0.7469 | 0.7526 | 1.01x |\\n\\n**解读要点**：008d 的低 obs gap ratio (1.30x) 具有误导性——其 dt=1 绝对误差本身已是 baseline 的 3x（模型已崩塌）。论文中必须并排呈现绝对误差和比率，避免审稿人被比率误导。\\n\\n**Strength**: Moderate-strong (D032 update: causal direction + diagnostic marker confirmed; collapse stochastic). The **nve>1.5x threshold** achieves 4/4 perfect separation: all trained dt_emb seeds (008d, 009b) exceed 1.5x; no untrained seeds (008f, 009c) exceed 1.5x. This is the paper's strongest quantitative result for C2. **Collapse** is stochastic (1/2 trained seeds): 008d seed 1 shows sustained nve>1.5x → collapse; 009b seed 2 shows transient nve>1.5x → self-correction. The **causal direction** is unambiguous across all 4 data points. Pending: 009e (008d seed 1) to determine collapse probability (1/3 vs 2/3); 009f (008f seed 1) for third untrained seed; 009c extension to 200K.\\n\\n### C3: Untrained dt_embedding prevents optimistic drift, substantively protecting performance\\n\\nWhen dt_embedding is untrained (random fixed), the value function cannot exploit precise dt information, preventing the optimistic value drift seen in trained variants. This value growth suppression substantively protects performance: exp_008a demonstrates two complete zigzag recovery cycles over 105K steps (peak @105K=778, 85% of baseline 916), with normalized v/e consistently suppressed at 0.59-0.93x baseline. The trained dt_embedding variant (exp_006) collapses catastrophically as its v/e ratio accelerates far past baseline levels (2.3x baseline@55K).\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| Two V-shaped recoveries (105K) | exp_008a (dt=2, subsample OFF, untrained dt_emb, H=15) | 501→563→488→608→470→584→572→778; two complete recovery cycles over 105K steps. @65K=608 (-1.3% baseline), @105K=778 (-15.1% baseline, 85% of 916). No collapse. |\\n| Sustained v/e suppression | exp_008a | v/e: 37.6%@55K → 37.2%@65K → 53.6%@75K → 47.5%@85K → 49.7%@95K → 38.6%@105K. Normalized v/e: 0.93x→0.66x→0.75x→0.68x→0.79x→0.59x baseline. Consistently below 1.0x, no acceleration. |\\n| Trained dt_emb: accelerating collapse | exp_006 (dt=2, subsample ON, trained dt_emb, H=15) | 485→477→360→collapse; v/e: 53.3%@45K (1.61x)→93.3%@55K (2.31x) → immediate collapse |\\n| v/e rate comparison (H=8 controlled) | exp_008c vs exp_008d | 008c (untrained): @35K=21.8% (0.90x)→@65K=32.8% (0.58x) (normalized declining); 008d (trained): @25K=15.5% (1.78x)→@35K=41.2% (1.71x) (normalized >1.5x = pathological). ~7x slower overestimation rate |\\n| Baseline v/e calibration | exp_001_baseline | v/e: 8.7%@25K → 24.1%@35K → 40.4%@55K → 56.3%@65K → 65.6%@105K (stable 69-72% from 135K+). 008a normalized v/e: 0.93x@55K → 0.66x@65K → 0.59x@105K (suppressed, diverging further below baseline); 008d: 1.7x@35K → 2.1x@45K (optimistic drift) |\\n\\n**Strength**: Strong (B+ confirmed with 105K long-run data). Two complete zigzag recovery cycles (501→608→470→778) with normalized v/e consistently 0.59-0.93x baseline across 105K steps. This is structural value growth suppression, not a transient delay. Contrasts sharply with exp_006's accelerating v/e (1.6x→2.3x baseline → collapse). The mechanism is clear: untrained dt_embedding prevents the value function from exploiting precise (but wrong) dt>1 predictions, suppressing the optimistic value drift that drives the CIVO feedback loop in trained variants.\\n\\n**Diagnostic metric: v/e overshoot ratio** = experiment v/e / baseline v/e at same training step. >1.5x = pathological warning. Trained dt_emb variants: 008d@35K=1.7x, @45K=2.1x; 006@45K=1.6x, @55K=2.3x. Untrained: 008a normalized v/e range 0.59-0.93x over 55K-105K (consistently below baseline = healthy, diverging further from baseline over time).\\n\\n**105K long-run confirmed**: exp_008a ran to 112K steps. Normalized v/e at 105K=0.59x baseline (lowest point), confirming value growth suppression is structural, not a transient delay. The suppression strengthens over time rather than converging to baseline levels.\\n\\n### C4: Longer dt amplifies the problem\\n\\nIncreasing dt from 2 to 4 worsens degradation, consistent with RSSM prediction error compounding over longer temporal gaps.\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| dt=2 degradation | exp_006_fixed_dt2 | Peak 485, collapse to ~135 |\\n| dt=4 severe degradation | exp_007_fixed_dt4 | Peak 176.9@25K, 144.4@45K (33% of baseline@45K=443) |\\n| Monotonic relationship | dt=1 (~950) > dt=2 (peak 485@35K) > dt=4 (peak 177@25K) | Clear monotonic decline |\\n\\n**Strength**: Moderate. Only two dt values tested (2 and 4). The monotonic trend is clear but a finer grid (dt=3, dt=6) would strengthen this claim. Sufficient for a supporting claim but not a standalone finding.\\n\\n### C5: Learning signal reduction from shorter effective horizons compounds degradation but is not the root cause\\n\\nSubsampling with dt>1 reduces the effective number of learning transitions per episode. This contributes to degradation but is neither necessary nor sufficient for collapse.\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| Subsample OFF, still degraded | exp_008c (subsample OFF, untrained dt_emb, H=8) | eval ~242 vs baseline ~950 |\\n| Subsample OFF, no collapse | exp_008a (subsample OFF, untrained dt_emb, H=15) | eval 778@105K (85% baseline), no collapse through 112K steps |\\n| Subsample ON, collapse | exp_008d (subsample ON, trained dt_emb, H=8) | eval 146, value overestimation |\\n| Horizon effect | exp_008c (H=8) vs exp_008a (H=15) | H=15 significantly outperforms H=8, both subsample OFF |\\n| Subsample ON, trained dt_emb, dt=1 imag, no collapse | exp_008e_v3 (subsample ON, trained dt_emb, dt=1 imag, H=15) | eval 382@45K (86% baseline); normalized v/e 0.88x@45K (normal). Even with trained dt_emb and subsample ON, restricting imagination to dt=1 prevents collapse |\\n\\n**Strength**: Moderate. The 008c vs 008a comparison shows horizon length matters independently. exp_008e_v3 confirms subsample ON does not trigger collapse when imagination is restricted to dt=1, even with trained dt_emb. But disentangling horizon from subsample effects requires additional controls. The key point—that it's not the root cause—is well-supported by 008c's stability despite lower performance.\\n\\n### C6: dt=1 imagination delays but does not eliminate CIVO collapse — the vulnerability is the trained dt_embedding itself\\n\\n**⚠️ D038 重大修正**: 008e_v3_s2 (seed=2) **崩溃** — eval 715@95K → 452 → 137@105K, nve=3.78x@105K, 全程 gate_dt_mean=1.0（dt=1 imagination 从未违反）。\\n\\n原假设\\\"dt=1 imagination = practical mitigation\\\"被**否证**。跨 seed 数据：\\n- seed 1: eval=869.9@105K ✓（95% baseline, nve=0.80x）\\n- seed 2: eval=137@105K ✗（崩溃, nve=3.78x）\\n- **独立 seed 崩溃率: 1/2 (50%)**\\n\\n对比 008d (trained dt_emb + dt=2 imagination): 同样 1/2 崩溃率（seed 1 collapse, seed 2 self-correct@268）。dt=1 imagination **未降低崩溃概率**。\\n\\n**⚠️ D039 机制辨析 — 008e_v3_s2 的崩溃可能不是 CIVO**\\n\\nReviewer 深度分析揭示 008e_v3_s2 与 008d 的崩溃动力学**定性不同**：\\n\\n| 特征 | 008d s1 (经典 CIVO) | 008e_v3_s2 (待确认) |\\n|------|---------------------|---------------------|\\n| value 变化 | 爆炸 (60→138, +130%@55K) | 温和 (339→384→340, +13%→-12%) |\\n| eval 变化 | 后跌 (146→83, -43%) | **先跌** (715→452→137, -81%) |\\n| nve 驱动 | value 分子驱动（value 爆炸） | eval 分母驱动（eval 崩溃） |\\n| actor_entropy | ↓ (-3.47→-4.88) 策略变确定 | **↑** (-5.21→-3.83) 策略变随机 |\\n| 机制 | critic overestimate → actor exploit | eval crash → value 滞后跟随 |\\n\\n**结论**: 008e_v3_s2 的 nve=3.78x 是 eval 崩溃的**结果**，不是 value overestimation 的**原因**。这更像 policy instability 而非 CIVO。\\n\\n**D040 最终判定**: 009a baseline seed 2 在 85-105K **完全稳定** (618→596→836, 正常波动后恢复)。排除 \\\"seed 2 本身不稳定\\\" 假说。**008e_v3_s2 的崩溃是配置导致的**。\\n\\n| Step | baseline s2 (009a) | 008e_v3 s2 | 差异 |\\n|------|-------------------|------------|------|\\n| 85K | 618.7 | 715.2 | 008e_v3 略高 |\\n| 95K | 596.2 (↓3.6%) | 452.4 (**↓37%**) | 10× 更大跌幅 |\\n| 105K | 836.5 (↑40%) | 137.0 (**↓70%**) | baseline 恢复 vs 008e_v3 继续崩 |\\n\\n**C6 最终状态: PARTIALLY FALSIFIED**\\n- dt=1 imagination 不能阻止崩溃（008e_v3: 1/2 seeds 崩溃 vs baseline: 0/2 seeds 崩溃）\\n- 崩溃是配置导致的，不是 seed 特异性\\n- 但崩溃**机制**与经典 CIVO 不同（见上方对比表）→ trained dt_embedding 可能通过**多条路径**创造脆弱性\\n\\n**论文表述建议**: \\\"Restricting imagination to dt=1 does not prevent collapse in the presence of trained dt-embedding (1/2 seeds collapse). While the collapse shares the high nve signature with classic CIVO, the underlying dynamics differ — the collapsed seed exhibits eval-driven destabilization with increasing policy entropy, rather than value-driven exploitation with decreasing entropy. This suggests trained dt-embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways, not solely through the value overestimation feedback loop.\\\"\\n\\n| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |\\n|----------|-----------|------------|\\n| dt=1 imag, seed 1, healthy | exp_008e_v3_walker_s1 (trained dt_emb, dt=1 imag, H=15) | eval=869.9@105K (95% baseline), nve=0.80x |\\n| **dt=1 imag, seed 2, COLLAPSED** | exp_008e_v3_walker_s2 (same config, seed=2) | eval 715@95K → 137@105K, nve ≤0.68x@85K → 1.34x@95K → **3.78x@105K**. gate_dt=1.0 throughout |\\n| dt=2 imag, seed 1, collapsed | exp_008d (trained dt_emb, dt=2 imag, H=8) | eval 167→82@55K, nve 1.78x@25K → 2.09x@45K. Onset at 25K |\\n| dt=2 imag, seed 2, self-corrected | exp_009b (008d config, seed 2) | eval 268@105K (rising), nve peak 1.62x@45K → self-correction |\\n| Onset delay | 008e_v3_s2 vs 008d | 008d onset nve>1.5x at 25-35K; 008e_v3_s2 at 95-105K. Delay ~70K steps |\\n| No dt_emb, stable | exp_008f (dt_embed_dim=0, subsample ON) | No collapse, reward_MAE 75x baseline |\\n| Untrained dt_emb, stable | exp_008a (untrained, subsample OFF, H=15) | 778@105K (85% baseline), nve 0.59-0.93x |\\n\\n**Strength**: **Moderate (D040: PARTIALLY FALSIFIED)** — dt=1 imagination 不能阻止崩溃 (1/2 seeds)，但崩溃机制与经典 CIVO 不同 (eval-driven vs value-driven)。009a baseline s2 稳定排除 seed 脆弱假说。核心洞察：trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways — CIVO (Pathway A, 008d) 和 non-CIVO policy instability (Pathway B, 008e_v3_s2)。dt=1 imagination 消除 Pathway A 但不消除 Pathway B。\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Story Arc\\n\\n### 1. Introduction\\n- Temporal abstraction is a long-sought goal in RL (options, macro-actions, skip connections)\\n- World-model RL (DreamerV3) offers a natural testbed: modify imagination dt without changing environment interaction\\n- Puzzle: all our attempts at variable-rate imagination degrade performance. Why?\\n- Contribution: systematic factorial diagnosis identifying trained dt_embedding as the reliable trigger for conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO, nve>1.5x), with collapse as a stochastic consequence. The vulnerability is deeper than imagination quality — even dt=1 imagination collapses at the same rate when dt_embedding is trained, revealing that training data dt>1 transitions alone drive the critic exploitation feedback loop\\n\\n### 2. Background & Related Work\\n- Temporal abstraction in model-free RL (options framework, FiGAR, action repeat)\\n- World-model RL (Dreamer family, IRIS, TWM)\\n- Variable-rate planning in world models (few prior works, mostly positive framing)\\n- Value overestimation in model-based RL (delusional bias per Lu et al. 2018 — differentiate from our CIVO)\\n\\n### 3. Introduction\\n- Temporal abstraction is a long-sought goal in RL (options, macro-actions, skip connections)\\n- World-model RL (DreamerV3) offers a natural testbed: modify imagination dt without changing environment interaction\\n- Puzzle: all our attempts at variable-rate imagination degrade performance. Why?\\n- Contribution: systematic factorial diagnosis identifying trained dt_embedding as the reliable trigger for conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO, nve>1.5x), with collapse as a stochastic consequence. The vulnerability is deeper than imagination quality — even dt=1 imagination collapses at the same rate when dt_embedding is trained, revealing that training data dt>1 transitions alone drive the critic exploitation feedback loop\\n\\n### 2. Background & Related Work\\n- Temporal abstraction in model-free RL (options framework, FiGAR, action repeat)\\n- World-model RL (Dreamer family, IRIS, TWM)\\n- Variable-rate planning in world models (few prior works, mostly positive framing)\\n- Value overestimation in model-based RL (delusional bias per Lu et al. 2018 — differentiate from our CIVO)\\n\\n### 3. Methodology\\n- DreamerV3 as base architecture\\n- Variable-rate imagination: dt_embedding, temporal subsampling, learned gating\\n- **Factorial experiment design**: 2×2×2 grid (dt_embedding trained/untrained × subsample ON/OFF × H=8/15) + baselines\\n- Diagnostic metrics: eval return, value/eval ratio as overestimation proxy, learning curves\\n\\n### 4. Results\\n- **Finding 1**: All dt>1 configurations degrade (C1)\\n- **Finding 2**: Controlled ablation isolates trained dt_embedding (C2) — the \\\"smoking gun\\\" comparison (008c vs 008d)\\n- **Finding 3**: Untrained dt_embedding prevents optimistic drift, sustaining near-baseline performance (C3)\\n- **Finding 4**: Longer dt amplifies (C4)\\n- **Finding 5**: Horizon/subsample effects are secondary (C5)\\n- **Finding 6 (partially falsified)**: dt=1 imagination does not prevent collapse (1/2 seeds), but collapsed seed (008e_v3_s2) shows non-CIVO dynamics (eval-driven, entropy ↑) unlike 008d's classic CIVO (value-driven, entropy ↓). 009a baseline s2 stable → collapse is config-caused. Trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways, not solely through value overestimation (C6, D040)\\n\\n### 5. Discussion\\n- Mechanism: why trained dt_embedding causes CIVO (RSSM fidelity gap at dt>1)\\n- RSSM fidelity analysis: 008d reward gap (2.78x) vs 008f reward gap (1.01x) — trained dt_emb 让 reward head 在 dt=2 时产生系统性偏差，这是 critic 被误导的直接来源\\n- 008f 的 reward 退化 trade-off：去掉 dt_embedding 避免崩塌但牺牲 reward 预测质量\\n- **D040: Multiple vulnerability pathways**: 008e_v3_s2 在 dt=1 imagination 下崩溃 (nve=3.78x@105K)，但机制与 008d 的 CIVO 不同：008d = value explosion → eval decline → entropy ↓；008e_v3_s2 = eval crash → value stable → entropy ↑。009a baseline s2 稳定排除 seed 脆弱。Trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways: Pathway A (CIVO, value-driven) requires dt>1 imagination; Pathway B (non-CIVO policy instability, eval-driven) operates independently of imagination dt\\n- Connection to existing theory: non-delusional Q-learning (Lu et al., 2018), model exploitation in MBRL\\n- Why this is specific to world-model RL (model-free temporal abstraction doesn't suffer the same failure mode)\\n- **D032: Value self-correction mechanism (009b)**: 009b (008d seed 2) demonstrates that pathological overestimation (nve>1.5x) is not always irreversible. Value peaked at 110.9@65K then monotonically self-corrected to 67.3@105K, while eval simultaneously improved (172→268). Hypothesized mechanism: when the critic's overestimation does not yet dominate the actor's gradient signal (transient vs sustained nve>1.5x), the actor can still learn from real environment returns, creating a corrective force. In 008d seed 1, the sustained overestimation (3 consecutive checkpoints >1.5x at 35K+) overwhelmed this correction. The bifurcation likely depends on early training stochasticity — initialization and data sampling order determine whether the overestimation feedback loop locks in before correction can take hold (consistent with primacy bias in MBRL, Qiao et al. 2023; early outlier runs, Bjorck et al. 2022). This makes nve>1.5x a **necessary condition** for collapse but not sufficient — the temporal persistence of overestimation is the second gate.\\n\\n### 6. Implications for Future Work\\n- **D038 update**: dt=1 imagination is NOT sufficient — trained dt_embedding in critic is the fundamental vulnerability, regardless of imagination strategy\\n- Don't use trained dt_embedding for temporal conditioning in imagination-based actor-critic training without safeguards (TAWM shows this works in MPC — the vulnerability is specific to imagination-based training)\\n- RSSM prediction quality must improve before variable-rate imagination is viable\\n- Potential safeguards: (a) ~~detach dt_embedding gradients from critic~~ **已实测否定（exp_016e: reward_dt_emb_detach=True, v/e=658%@95K）— SGS 延迟崩溃 ~50K 步并提高峰值 2x（327 vs 167），说明 reward 梯度通路是贡献因素之一，但阻断它不足以防止 CIVO。根因在 representation level：world model training 本身将 dt>1 dynamics 编码进 dt_emb，使 critic 在 imagination 中系统性高估。**, (b) stop-gradient on dt>1 critic targets, (c) pessimistic value ensemble for dt>1 transitions, (d) uncertainty-gated truncation\\n- Need for diagnostic methodology in temporal abstraction research\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n### R1: \\\"Limited to one environment / one base algorithm\\\"\\n**Pre-emption**: Our claims are mechanistic (trained dt_embedding → value overestimation → collapse). ## Title Candidates

1. **"Why Temporal Abstraction Fails in DreamerV3: A Diagnostic Analysis of Variable-Rate Imagination"**
2. ~~**"The Delusional Critic Problem in DreamerV3's Variable-Rate Imagination"**~~ (deprecated — "delusional critic" conflicts with Lu et al. 2018)
3. **"Diagnosing Value Overestimation from Temporal Abstraction in DreamerV3"** ← preferred after D037 terminology decision
4. **"Conditioning-Induced Value Overestimation in Variable-Rate World-Model Imagination"**

**⚠️ D037 术语决定**: "delusional critic" → **"conditioning-induced value overestimation"** (简称 CIVO)。Lu et al. 2018 的 delusional bias 指 policy-class constraints 导致不可实现的 Q 值，本文机制是 model imprecision + learned conditioning amplification，概念不同。Dream 模拟三档审稿一致指出术语误导。全文替换："delusional critic" → "conditioning-induced value overestimation"，可 cite Lu et al. 2018 as analogy but must explicitly differentiate。

**⚠️ D037 TAWM 对比（关键 novelty 升级）**: TAWM (Nhu et al., ICML 2025) 在 TD-MPC2 (MPC setting) 中成功使用 dt-conditioning。本文发现 dt-conditioning 在 imagination-based actor-critic 中失败 → **novelty 从 "known failure class 的 specific instance" 升级为 "dt-conditioning succeeds in MPC but fails in imagination — here's the architecture-specific vulnerability"**。TAWM 是强化 novelty 的最关键参考文献。

## Venue

**CoRL 2026** — Deadline: 2026-05-29

## Narrative Positioning

This is a **diagnostic analysis paper**, not a method paper. We do not propose a new algorithm. Instead, we provide a systematic, controlled investigation answering: *Why does temporal abstraction fail in world-model RL?*

The contribution is a **strongly supported causal chain** from mechanism to failure mode, backed by a factorial experiment design that isolates each factor, plus a **practical mitigation guideline** (restrict imagination to dt=1 during multi-dt training → 95% baseline recovery). Diagnostic papers are valued when they (a) address a widely-attempted but poorly-understood failure, (b) provide actionable insight for future method design, and (c) are methodologically rigorous.

We scope all claims to **DreamerV3 and its RSSM world model**. Generalizability to other latent-dynamics architectures is discussed but not claimed.

---

## Core Claims

### C1: Variable-rate imagination in DreamerV3 consistently degrades performance

Temporal abstraction via variable dt—whether learned or fixed—degrades asymptotic performance relative to the dt=1 baseline across all tested configurations.

| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Baseline stability | exp_001_baseline (dt=1) | Stable convergence ~950 eval return |
| Fixed dt=2 collapse | exp_006_fixed_dt2 (dt=2, subsample ON, H=15) | Peak 485@35K → collapse to ~135@65K |
| Fixed dt=4 severe degradation | exp_007_fixed_dt4 (dt=4) | Peak 176.9@25K, 144.4@45K (33% of baseline@45K=443) |
| Learned gate collapse | exp_005 (learned gate) | Peak 541@55K → 99@145K |

**Strength**: Strong. Three independent dt>1 configurations all show degradation. No positive result exists for variable-rate imagination in our setup.

### C2: Trained dt_embedding reliably triggers pathological value overestimation (>1.5x), creating high collapse risk

**D032 update: nve>1.5x threshold has perfect separating power (4/4); collapse itself is stochastic.**

The trained dt_embedding reliably induces pathological value overestimation (normalized v/e >1.5x baseline) across all tested seeds, but whether this overestimation progresses to catastrophic performance collapse is stochastic:

- **WITH trained dt_emb**: 2/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x at 35K+ (008d seed 1: sustained 1.71x@35K→2.09x@45K→4.12x@55K → collapse; 009b seed 2: 1.62x@45K → self-correction to 0.38x@105K)
- **WITHOUT dt_emb (008f)**: 0/2 seeds exceed nve>1.5x at 35K+ (seed 1 peak 1.02x@25K; seed 2 peak 1.26x@25K)
- **1.5x threshold (35K+)**: 4/4 perfect classification — reliable diagnostic marker separating trained vs untrained dt_emb

**⚠️ 时间限定**: nve>1.5x 诊断适用于 **35K+ steps**（此时 baseline v/e 已充分收敛至 >0.24，比率稳定可靠）。25K 处 baseline v/e 仅 0.087，微小绝对差异可被放大为大比率（如 009b@25K nve=2.05x 和 008e_v3@25K nve=1.93x 均为 false positive）。论文中报告 threshold 时必须标注此限定。

**Sustained vs transient overestimation**: The key difference between collapse (008d seed 1) and self-correction (009b seed 2) is the **temporal persistence** of nve>1.5x. Seed 1 maintained nve>1.5x across 3 consecutive checkpoints at 35K+ (1.71x@35K→2.09x@45K→4.12x@55K, accelerating), locking the positive feedback loop; seed 2 exceeded 1.5x at 45K (1.62x) but dropped to 1.41x@55K and continued declining, allowing self-correction. This suggests a "point of no return" where sustained overestimation becomes irreversible, with early training stochasticity (initialization, data sampling order) determining which path is taken (cf. Henderson et al. 2018, Bjorck et al. 2022, Qiao et al. 2023).

The trained dt_embedding enables precise dt prediction in imagination, but RSSM state prediction quality at dt>1 is insufficient to support this precision. The result is conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO) that drives actor learning toward incorrect policies. Without dt_embedding conditioning, the overestimation feedback loop is blocked entirely (nve never exceeds 1.5x).

|----------|-----------|------------|

**Strength**: Moderate-strong (D032 update: causal direction + diagnostic marker confirmed; collapse stochastic). The **nve>1.5x threshold** achieves 4/4 perfect separation: all trained dt_emb seeds (008d, 009b) exceed 1.5x; no untrained seeds (008f, 009c) exceed 1.5x. This is the paper's strongest quantitative result for C2. **Collapse** is stochastic (1/2 trained seeds): 008d seed 1 shows sustained nve>1.5x → collapse; 009b seed 2 shows transient nve>1.5x → self-correction. The **causal direction** is unambiguous across all 4 data points. Pending: 009e (008d seed 1) to determine collapse probability (1/3 vs 2/3); 009f (008f seed 1) for third untrained seed; 009c extension to 200K.

### C3: Untrained dt_embedding prevents optimistic drift, substantively protecting performance

When dt_embedding is untrained (random fixed), the value function cannot exploit precise dt information, preventing the optimistic value drift seen in trained variants. This value growth suppression substantively protects performance: exp_008a demonstrates two complete zigzag recovery cycles over 105K steps (peak @105K=778, 85% of baseline 916), with normalized v/e consistently suppressed at 0.59-0.93x baseline. The trained dt_embedding variant (exp_006) collapses catastrophically as its v/e ratio accelerates far past baseline levels (2.3x baseline@55K).

| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Two V-shaped recoveries (105K) | exp_008a (dt=2, subsample OFF, untrained dt_emb, H=15) | 501→563→488→608→470→584→572→778; two complete recovery cycles over 105K steps. @65K=608 (-1.3% baseline), @105K=778 (-15.1% baseline, 85% of 916). No collapse. |
| Sustained v/e suppression | exp_008a | v/e: 37.6%@55K → 37.2%@65K → 53.6%@75K → 47.5%@85K → 49.7%@95K → 38.6%@105K. Normalized v/e: 0.93x→0.66x→0.75x→0.68x→0.79x→0.59x baseline. Consistently below 1.0x, no acceleration. |
| Trained dt_emb: accelerating collapse | exp_006 (dt=2, subsample ON, trained dt_emb, H=15) | 485→477→360→collapse; v/e: 53.3%@45K (1.61x)→93.3%@55K (2.31x) → immediate collapse |
| v/e rate comparison (H=8 controlled) | exp_008c vs exp_008d | 008c (untrained): @35K=21.8% (0.90x)→@65K=32.8% (0.58x) (normalized declining); 008d (trained): @25K=15.5% (1.78x)→@35K=41.2% (1.71x) (normalized >1.5x = pathological). ~7x slower overestimation rate |
| Baseline v/e calibration | exp_001_baseline | v/e: 8.7%@25K → 24.1%@35K → 40.4%@55K → 56.3%@65K → 65.6%@105K (stable 69-72% from 135K+). 008a normalized v/e: 0.93x@55K → 0.66x@65K → 0.59x@105K (suppressed, diverging further below baseline); 008d: 1.7x@35K → 2.1x@45K (optimistic drift) |

**Strength**: Strong (B+ confirmed with 105K long-run data). Two complete zigzag recovery cycles (501→608→470→778) with normalized v/e consistently 0.59-0.93x baseline across 105K steps. This is structural value growth suppression, not a transient delay. Contrasts sharply with exp_006's accelerating v/e (1.6x→2.3x baseline → collapse). **Diagnostic metric: v/e overshoot ratio** = experiment v/e / baseline v/e at same training step. >1.5x = pathological warning. Trained dt_emb variants: 008d@35K=1.7x, @45K=2.1x; 006@45K=1.6x, @55K=2.3x. Untrained: 008a normalized v/e range 0.59-0.93x over 55K-105K (consistently below baseline = healthy, diverging further from baseline over time).

**105K long-run confirmed**: exp_008a ran to 112K steps. Normalized v/e at 105K=0.59x baseline (lowest point), confirming value growth suppression is structural, not a transient delay. The suppression strengthens over time rather than converging to baseline levels.

Increasing dt from 2 to 4 worsens degradation, consistent with RSSM prediction error compounding over longer temporal gaps.

| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |

| Monotonic relationship | dt=1 (~950) > dt=2 (peak 485@35K) > dt=4 (peak 177@25K) | Clear monotonic decline |

**Strength**: Moderate. Only two dt values tested (2 and 4). The monotonic trend is clear but a finer grid (dt=3, dt=6) would strengthen this claim. Sufficient for a supporting claim but not a standalone finding.

### C5: Learning signal reduction from shorter effective horizons compounds degradation but is not the root cause

Subsampling with dt>1 reduces the effective number of learning transitions per episode. This contributes to degradation but is neither necessary nor sufficient for collapse.

| Evidence | Experiment | Key Metric |

---

## Story Arc

### 1. Introduction
- Temporal abstraction is a long-sought goal in RL (options, macro-actions, skip connections)
- World-model RL (DreamerV3) offers a natural testbed: modify imagination dt without changing environment interaction
- Puzzle: all our attempts at variable-rate imagination degrade performance. Why?
- Contribution: systematic factorial diagnosis identifying trained dt_embedding as the reliable trigger for conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO, nve>1.5x), with collapse as a stochastic consequence. The vulnerability is deeper than imagination quality — even dt=1 imagination collapses at the same rate when dt_embedding is trained, revealing that training data dt>1 transitions alone drive the critic exploitation feedback loop

### 2. Background & Related Work
- Temporal abstraction in model-free RL (options framework, FiGAR, action repeat)
- World-model RL (Dreamer family, IRIS, TWM)
- Variable-rate planning in world models (few prior works, mostly positive framing)
- Value overestimation in model-based RL (delusional bias per Lu et al. 2018 — differentiate from our CIVO)

### 3. Methodology
- DreamerV3 as base architecture
- Variable-rate imagination: dt_embedding, temporal subsampling, learned gating
- **Factorial experiment design**: 2×2×2 grid (dt_embedding trained/untrained × subsample ON/OFF × H=8/15) + baselines
- Diagnostic metrics: eval return, value/eval ratio as overestimation proxy, learning curves

### 4. Results
- **Finding 1**: All dt>1 configurations degrade (C1)
- **Finding 2**: Controlled ablation isolates trained dt_embedding (C2) — the "smoking gun" comparison (008c vs 008d)
- **Finding 3**: Untrained dt_embedding prevents optimistic drift, sustaining near-baseline performance (C3)
- **Finding 4**: Longer dt amplifies (C4)
- **Finding 5**: Horizon/subsample effects are secondary (C5)
- **Finding 6 (partially falsified)**: dt=1 imagination does not prevent collapse (1/2 seeds), but collapsed seed (008e_v3_s2) shows non-CIVO dynamics (eval-driven, entropy ↑) unlike 008d's classic CIVO (value-driven, entropy ↓). 009a baseline s2 stable → collapse is config-caused. Trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways, not solely through value overestimation (C6, D040)

### 5. Discussion
- Mechanism: why trained dt_embedding causes CIVO (RSSM fidelity gap at dt>1)
- RSSM fidelity analysis: 008d reward gap (2.78x) vs 008f reward gap (1.01x) — trained dt_emb 让 reward head 在 dt=2 时产生系统性偏差，这是 critic 被误导的直接来源
- 008f 的 reward 退化 trade-off：去掉 dt_embedding 避免崩塌但牺牲 reward 预测质量
- **D040: Multiple vulnerability pathways**: 008e_v3_s2 在 dt=1 imagination 下崩溃 (nve=3.78x@105K)，但机制与 008d 的 CIVO 不同：008d = value explosion → eval decline → entropy ↓；008e_v3_s2 = eval crash → value stable → entropy ↑。009a baseline s2 稳定排除 seed 脆弱。Trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways: Pathway A (CIVO, value-driven) requires dt>1 imagination; Pathway B (non-CIVO policy instability, eval-driven) operates independently of imagination dt
- Connection to existing theory: non-delusional Q-learning (Lu et al., 2018), model exploitation in MBRL
- Why this is specific to world-model RL (model-free temporal abstraction doesn't suffer the same failure mode)
- **D032: Value self-correction mechanism (009b)**: 009b (008d seed 2) demonstrates that pathological overestimation (nve>1.5x) is not always irreversible. Value peaked at 110.9@65K then monotonically self-corrected to 67.3@105K, while eval simultaneously improved (172→268). Hypothesized mechanism: when the critic's overestimation does not yet dominate the actor's gradient signal (transient vs sustained nve>1.5x), the actor can still learn from real environment returns, creating a corrective force. In 008d seed 1, the sustained overestimation (3 consecutive checkpoints >1.5x at 35K+) overwhelmed this correction. The bifurcation likely depends on early training stochasticity — initialization and data sampling order determine whether the overestimation feedback loop locks in before correction can take hold (consistent with primacy bias in MBRL, Qiao et al. 2023; early outlier runs, Bjorck et al. 2022). This makes nve>1.5x a **necessary condition** for collapse but not sufficient — the temporal persistence of overestimation is the second gate.

### 6. Implications for Future Work
- **D038 update**: dt=1 imagination is NOT sufficient — trained dt_embedding in critic is the fundamental vulnerability, regardless of imagination strategy
- Don't use trained dt_embedding for temporal conditioning in imagination-based actor-critic training without safeguards (TAWM shows this works in MPC — the vulnerability is specific to imagination-based training)
- RSSM prediction quality must improve before variable-rate imagination is viable
- Potential safeguards: (a) ~~detach dt_embedding gradients from critic~~ **已实测否定（exp_016e: reward_dt_emb_detach=True, v/e=658%@95K）— SGS 延迟崩溃 ~50K 步并提高峰值 2x（327 vs 167），说明 reward 梯度通路是贡献因素之一，但阻断它不足以防止 CIVO。根因在 representation level：world model training 本身将 dt>1 dynamics 编码进 dt_emb，使 critic 在 imagination 中系统性高估。**, (b) stop-gradient on dt>1 critic targets, (c) pessimistic value ensemble for dt>1 transitions, (d) uncertainty-gated truncation
- Need for diagnostic methodology in temporal abstraction research

---

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### R1: "Limited to one environment / one base algorithm"
**Pre-emption**: Our claims are mechanistic (trained dt_embedding → value overestimation → collapse). The causal chain is architecture-specific by design—we diagnose *why* it fails in DreamerV3, not whether it fails everywhere. The mechanism (RSSM fidelity gap) likely generalizes to other latent-dynamics models but we scope claims conservatively.
**Mitigation**: Cheetah Run is a planned experiment in our experiment schedule, not a stretch goal. We will include at least one additional DMC environment (Cheetah Run) to demonstrate generality of the mechanism.

### R2: "No proposed solution — what's the actionable takeaway?"
**Pre-emption**: Our primary contribution is diagnostic, not prescriptive. The causal chain (C1-C5) provides clear guidance: trained dt_embedding is the necessary condition for CIVO. Restricting imagination to dt=1 eliminates CIVO (Pathway A) but not all failure modes — 008e_v3 shows 1/2 seeds collapse via a distinct non-CIVO pathway (eval-driven policy instability). The actionable takeaway is that trained dt_embedding creates vulnerability through multiple pathways in imagination-based actor-critic; surface-level fixes are insufficient. Hierarchical approaches (THICK, Hieros) that avoid flat dt-conditioning are the recommended direction.
**Mitigation**: Present the dual-pathway finding as a key diagnostic contribution (Section 5). dt=1 imagination is a partial mitigation (eliminates CIVO) but not robust (1/2 collapse via Pathway B).

### R3: "Value/eval ratio is a crude proxy for overestimation"
**Pre-emption**: We acknowledge this is a proxy, not a formal divergence measure. However, the v/e overshoot ratio (experiment v/e / baseline v/e at same step) consistently identifies pathological overestimation: trained dt_emb variants exceed 1.5x baseline v/e before collapse, while untrained variants stay at or below baseline levels.
**Mitigation**: Add distributional analysis of value predictions vs. realized returns if time permits.

### R4: "The factorial design is incomplete — missing cells in the grid"
**Pre-emption**: We prioritized the most informative comparisons. The 008c vs 008d pair isolates dt_embedding training with all else held constant—this is the critical controlled experiment.
**Mitigation**: Explicitly present the factorial grid, mark which cells are filled, and justify the prioritization.

### R5: "Novelty concern — model exploitation / value overestimation in MBRL is well-known"
**Pre-emption**: General MBRL overestimation is known (Janner et al., 2019), but the specific mechanism through temporal abstraction's dt_embedding is novel. Prior work on temporal abstraction in world models has not identified this failure mode. Our contribution is the *specific causal link*, not the general phenomenon.

### R6: "All results from a single seed — how robust are the conclusions?"
**Pre-emption (D032 update)**: Multi-seed data now available. The nve>1.5x diagnostic threshold achieves **4/4 perfect classification** across seeds: trained dt_emb (008d seed 1, 009b seed 2) both exceed 1.5x; untrained (008f seed 1, 009c seed 2) neither exceeds 1.5x. Collapse itself is stochastic (1/2 trained seeds), which we report transparently — our claim is about the reliable **diagnostic marker** (nve>1.5x), not deterministic collapse.
**[D040]** C6 partially falsified: 008e_v3_s2 collapsed via non-CIVO pathway (eval-driven, entropy ↑). 009a baseline s2 stable (618→596→836) — rules out seed fragility. Trained dt_embedding creates multiple vulnerability pathways: CIVO (Pathway A, 008d) and policy instability (Pathway B, 008e_v3_s2). dt=1 imagination eliminates Pathway A but not B.
**Mitigation**: Report all seeds with IQM + confidence intervals per Agarwal et al. (2021). The 4/4 separation is robust. Additional seeds (009e, 009f) pending to further narrow collapse probability estimates.

### R7: "The factorial design confounds dt_embedding training with training data composition"
**Pre-emption**: exp_008f confirmed: dt_embed_dim=0 + subsample ON → normalized v/e 0.83x@45K (healthy), vs 008d@45K=2.09x (collapse at v/e=69.3%). This confirms dt_embedding conditioning—not RSSM learned dynamics—is the causal mechanism. exp_008f uses identical training data composition as 008d (subsample ON, dt=2 transitions) but removes dt_embedding conditioning. Through 55K, 008f remained in normal range (normalized v/e 0.73-1.02x).
**Mitigation**: The 008f causal control resolves this confound definitively. The three-way comparison (008c: subsample OFF/untrained, 008d: subsample ON/trained, 008f: subsample ON/no dt_embed) isolates dt_embedding conditioning as the necessary and sufficient factor for CIVO.

### R8: "008f reward prediction degradation undermines the causal control"
**Pre-emption**: 008f 的 reward_MAE=0.747（baseline 75x）是重要发现，但不削弱 C2 因果结论。008f 证明的是"去掉 dt_embedding → 不崩塌"，这个 collapse vs no-collapse 的区分不依赖 reward 质量。008f 的低 v/e 部分源于奖励噪声，但关键对比是 008d 的 v/e 加速发散 vs 008f 的 v/e 保持稳定——模式差异才是因果证据。
**Mitigation**: 论文中明确区分 008f 的角色（因果控制实验）和 008e_v3 的角色（诊断证据：dt=1 imagination 不能消除 CIVO）。RSSM fidelity 表同时报告绝对误差和比率，避免审稿人被 008d 的低 obs gap ratio（1.30x，但绝对误差 41.31 已是 baseline 3x）误导。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fig 3: NVE Diagnostic — Task B2 CIVO detection (D054 corrected).
008e_v3_s2 reclassified as non-CIVO (IRD), shown as FP.
"""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import os

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 9.5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.05,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.8,
})

tp = [('006', 4.84), ('008d', 4.13), ('009b', 1.62)]
tn = [('001', 1.00), ('008a', 0.93), ('008f', 0.97), ('008e_v3_s1', 0.94)]
fp = [('008e_v3_s2', 3.78)]
THRESHOLD = 1.5

all_points = []
for name, nve in tn:
    all_points.append((name, nve, 'TN'))
for name, nve in fp:
    all_points.append((name, nve, 'FP'))
for name, nve in tp:
    all_points.append((name, nve, 'TP'))
all_points.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])

labels = [p[0] for p in all_points]
nves   = [p[1] for p in all_points]
types  = [p[2] for p in all_points]
y_pos  = np.arange(len(all_points))

COLOR_TP = '#C0392B'
COLOR_TN = '#2471A3'
COLOR_FP = '#E67E22'

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))

ax.axvspan(0, THRESHOLD, alpha=0.06, color=COLOR_TN, zorder=0)
ax.axvspan(THRESHOLD, 5.8, alpha=0.06, color=COLOR_TP, zorder=0)
ax.axvline(x=THRESHOLD, color='#7F8C8D', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)

for i, (name, nve, tp_type) in enumerate(all_points):
    if tp_type == 'TP':
        color, marker, ms = COLOR_TP, 'o', 9
    elif tp_type == 'FP':
        color, marker, ms = COLOR_FP, 'D', 9
    else:
        color, marker, ms = COLOR_TN, 's', 8

    ax.plot(nve, i, marker=marker, color=color, markersize=ms,
            markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.2, zorder=4)
    ax.plot([0, nve], [i, i], color=color, linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.35, zorder=2)

    if tp_type == 'FP':
        ax.annotate('FP (IRD, non-CIVO)',
                     xy=(nve, i), xytext=(nve + 0.15, i - 0.7),
                     fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold', color=COLOR_FP,
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=COLOR_FP, lw=1.2),
                     zorder=5)

ax.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax.set_yticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, family='monospace')
ax.set_xlabel('Normalized Value Excess (NVE)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_xlim(-0.15, 5.8)
ax.set_ylim(-1.0, len(all_points) + 0.2)

ax.text(THRESHOLD / 2, len(all_points) + 0.05, 'Non-CIVO',
        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color=COLOR_TN, alpha=0.6,
        fontweight='bold')
ax.text(THRESHOLD + (5.8 - THRESHOLD) / 2, len(all_points) + 0.05,
        'CIVO-positive',
        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color=COLOR_TP, alpha=0.6,
        fontweight='bold')

h_tp = plt.Line2D([], [], marker='o', color=COLOR_TP, markersize=8,
                   markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1, linestyle='None',
                   label='True CIVO (TP)')
h_tn = plt.Line2D([], [], marker='s', color=COLOR_TN, markersize=7,
                   markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1, linestyle='None',
                   label='Non-CIVO (TN)')
h_fp = plt.Line2D([], [], marker='D', color=COLOR_FP, markersize=8,
                   markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1, linestyle='None',
                   label='False Positive (FP)')
h_th = plt.Line2D([], [], color='#7F8C8D', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2,
                   label=f'Threshold ({THRESHOLD}x)')
ax.legend(handles=[h_tp, h_tn, h_fp, h_th], loc='upper left',
          fontsize=9, framealpha=0.92, edgecolor='#BDC3C7')

stats_text = (
    'AUROC = 0.933   CI [0.47, 1.0]\n'
    'Accuracy = 7/8 (87.5%)\n'
    r'Task B2: NVE $\geq$ 1.5$\times$ @ 35K+'
    '\n(Clopper–Pearson, 95%)'
)
ax.text(0.98, 0.03, stats_text, transform=ax.transAxes,
        ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9.5,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#FAFAFA',
                  edgecolor='#BDC3C7', alpha=0.95))

ax.set_title('NVE Diagnostic: CIVO Detection (D054 Corrected)', fontsize=13,
             fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.15, axis='x', zorder=0)

plt.tight_layout()

outdir = os.environ.get('OUTDIR', '.')
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig3_nve_diagnostic_d054.pdf')
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig3_nve_diagnostic_d054.png')
plt.close()
print(f'Saved: {outdir}/fig3_nve_diagnostic_d054.pdf')
print(f'Saved: {outdir}/fig3_nve_diagnostic_d054.png')

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrowPatch
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from fig_style import apply_style
apply_style()

# --- Data ---
# 008d s1 (Pathway A — CIVO)
steps_008d = np.array([25000, 35000, 45000, 55000])
eval_008d = np.array([167.22, 146.34, 140.80, 82.75])
value_008d = np.array([25.86, 60.20, 97.50, 137.88])
entropy_008d = np.array([-3.47, -3.91, -4.35, -4.88])

# 008e_v3 s2 (Pathway B — Non-CIVO)
steps_008e = np.array([5000, 15000, 25000, 35000, 45000, 55000, 65000, 75000, 85000, 95000, 105000])
eval_008e = np.array([39.27, 180.85, 211.82, 320.39, 356.93, 418.32, 435.09, 576.54, 715.21, 452.43, 136.96])
value_008e = np.array([0, 3.91, 30.27, 79.75, 125.25, 172.89, 220.47, 272.64, 339.30, 384.39, 339.84])
entropy_008e = np.array([8.239, 2.352, 0.17, -3.498, -4.915, -5.121, -5.135, -5.224, -5.208, -4.529, -3.828])

# 009a baseline s2 (Control)
steps_baseline = np.array([5000, 15000, 25000, 35000, 45000, 55000, 65000, 75000, 85000, 95000, 105000])
eval_baseline = np.array([41.21, 106.01, 325.33, 354.49, 498.01, 534.13, 688.87, 656.85, 618.73, 596.24, 836.51])
value_baseline_sparse = {5000: 0, 25000: 45.78, 55000: 253.49, 105000: 539.34}

# Interpolate baseline value for smooth line
vb_steps = np.array(sorted(value_baseline_sparse.keys()))
vb_values = np.array([value_baseline_sparse[s] for s in vb_steps])

# Colors
C_MAIN = '#D55E00'
C_BASE = '#999999'
C_COLLAPSE_BG = '#FFCCCC'

# Convert steps to K for display
def to_k(steps):
    return steps / 1000

# --- Figure ---
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(3, 2, hspace=0.38, wspace=0.32,
                       top=0.88, bottom=0.11, left=0.09, right=0.97)

row_labels = ['Eval Return', 'Value Mean', 'Actor Entropy']

# Column titles
fig.text(0.295, 0.945, 'Pathway A: CIVO (008d s1)', ha='center', va='bottom',
         fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', color=C_MAIN)
fig.text(0.295, 0.925, r'$dt{=}2$ imagination, trained $dt$-emb  |  NVE = 4.13',
         ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, color='#555555')

fig.text(0.745, 0.945, 'Pathway B: Non-CIVO (008e_v3 s2)', ha='center', va='bottom',
         fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', color=C_MAIN)
fig.text(0.745, 0.925, r'$dt{=}1$ imagination, trained $dt$-emb  |  NVE = 3.78 (FP — IRD)',
         ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, color='#555555')

# ============================================================
# Column A (left) — 008d s1
# ============================================================

# Baseline clipped to Pathway A range for reference
mask_bl_a = (steps_baseline >= 25000) & (steps_baseline <= 55000)
steps_bl_a = steps_baseline[mask_bl_a]
eval_bl_a = eval_baseline[mask_bl_a]

# --- Row 1: Eval Return ---
ax_a1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
ax_a1.plot(to_k(steps_bl_a), eval_bl_a, '--', color=C_BASE, linewidth=1.5, label='009a baseline', zorder=1)
ax_a1.plot(to_k(steps_008d), eval_008d, '-o', color=C_MAIN, markersize=5, label='008d s1', zorder=2)
ax_a1.axvspan(to_k(35000), to_k(55000), alpha=0.12, color='red', zorder=0)
ax_a1.set_ylabel('Eval Return')
ax_a1.set_xlim(22, 58)
ax_a1.legend(loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
# Annotation: eval decline arrow
ax_a1.annotate('eval decline',
               xy=(55, 82.75), xytext=(38, 60),
               fontsize=9, color='#B00000', fontweight='bold',
               arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#B00000', lw=1.5),
               ha='center')

# --- Row 2: Value Mean ---
ax_a2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
# baseline value sparse points in range
mask_vb_a = (vb_steps >= 25000) & (vb_steps <= 55000)
ax_a2.plot(to_k(vb_steps[mask_vb_a]), vb_values[mask_vb_a], '--', color=C_BASE, linewidth=1.5, label='009a baseline', zorder=1)
ax_a2.plot(to_k(steps_008d), value_008d, '-o', color=C_MAIN, markersize=5, label='008d s1', zorder=2)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fig 3: Factorial experiment summary — 2×2 grid + control annotation.
Rows: Subsample (OFF/ON), Cols: Horizon (H=15/H=8).
All cells use trained dt_embedding. Control (008f, no dt_emb) annotated separately.
"""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from fig_style import apply_style
apply_style()

BASELINE_EVAL = 915.67

grid_data = {
    (0, 0): {'config': '008a', 'eval': 777.7, 'nve': 0.59, 'step': '105K',
             'collapsed': False, 'h': 15, 'sub': 'OFF'},
    (0, 1): {'config': '008c', 'eval': 240.9, 'nve': 0.58, 'step': '65K',
             'collapsed': False, 'h': 8, 'sub': 'OFF'},
    (1, 0): {'config': '006',  'eval': 132.9, 'nve': 4.83, 'step': '65K',
             'collapsed': True, 'h': 15, 'sub': 'ON'},
    (1, 1): {'config': '008d', 'eval': 82.8,  'nve': 4.12, 'step': '55K',
             'collapsed': True, 'h': 8, 'sub': 'ON'},
}

control = {'config': '008f', 'eval': 503.0, 'nve': 0.30, 'step': '105K',
           'label': 'No dt_emb\n(control)'}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5))
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 3.8)
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, 2.5)
ax.axis('off')

cell_w, cell_h = 1.3, 0.9
x_offsets = [0, 1.5]
y_offsets = [1.2, 0]

col_labels = ['H = 15', 'H = 8']
row_labels = ['Subsample OFF', 'Subsample ON']

for ci, xl in enumerate(col_labels):
    ax.text(x_offsets[ci] + cell_w / 2, y_offsets[0] + cell_h + 0.15, xl,
            ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

for ri, rl in enumerate(row_labels):
    ax.text(x_offsets[0] - 0.12, y_offsets[ri] + cell_h / 2, rl,
            ha='right', va='center', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', rotation=0)

for (row, col), d in grid_data.items():
    x = x_offsets[col]
    y = y_offsets[row]

    if d['collapsed']:
        bg_color = '#FDEDEC'
        border_color = '#E74C3C'
        status_symbol = r'$\times$'
        status_color = '#C0392B'
    else:
        bg_color = '#EAFAF1'
        border_color = '#27AE60'
        status_symbol = r'$\checkmark$'
        status_color = '#1E8449'

    rect = mpatches.FancyBboxPatch(
        (x, y), cell_w, cell_h,
        boxstyle='round,pad=0.05',
        facecolor=bg_color, edgecolor=border_color, linewidth=2)
    ax.add_patch(rect)

    pct = d['eval'] / BASELINE_EVAL * 100
    ax.text(x + cell_w / 2, y + cell_h * 0.72,
            f"{d['config']}",
            ha='center', va='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#333')
    ax.text(x + cell_w / 2, y + cell_h * 0.48,
            f"eval = {d['eval']:.0f}  ({pct:.0f}%)",
            ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color='#333')
    ax.text(x + cell_w / 2, y + cell_h * 0.25,
            f"nve = {d['nve']:.2f}×  {status_symbol}",
            ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color=status_color,
            fontweight='bold')

ctrl_x = x_offsets[1] + cell_w + 0.45
ctrl_y = y_offsets[1]
ctrl_w, ctrl_h = 1.15, cell_h

ctrl_rect = mpatches.FancyBboxPatch(
    (ctrl_x, ctrl_y), ctrl_w, ctrl_h,
    boxstyle='round,pad=0.05',
    facecolor='#EBF5FB', edgecolor='#2980B9', linewidth=2, linestyle='--')
ax.add_patch(ctrl_rect)

ax.text(ctrl_x + ctrl_w / 2, ctrl_y + ctrl_h * 0.78,
        control['label'], ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9.5,
        fontweight='bold', color='#2471A3')
ax.text(ctrl_x + ctrl_w / 2, ctrl_y + ctrl_h * 0.45,
        f"eval = {control['eval']:.0f}  ({control['eval']/BASELINE_EVAL*100:.0f}%)",
        ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9, color='#2471A3')
ax.text(ctrl_x + ctrl_w / 2, ctrl_y + ctrl_h * 0.22,
        f"nve = {control['nve']:.2f}×  " + r"$\checkmark$",
        ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9, color='#1E8449', fontweight='bold')

ax.annotate('', xy=(x_offsets[1] + cell_w + 0.05, y_offsets[1] + cell_h / 2),
            xytext=(ctrl_x - 0.05, ctrl_y + ctrl_h / 2),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#7F8C8D', lw=1.5,
                            connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0'))
ax.text((x_offsets[1] + cell_w + ctrl_x) / 2, y_offsets[1] - 0.12,
        'same config,\nminus trained dt_emb',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=8.5, color='#7F8C8D', style='italic')

ax.axhline(y=y_offsets[0] - 0.15, xmin=0.02, xmax=0.65, color='#BDC3C7',
           linewidth=0.8, linestyle='-')

ax.text((x_offsets[0] + x_offsets[1] + cell_w) / 2, y_offsets[0] + cell_h + 0.45,
        'Factorial Design: Trained dt_embedding × Subsample × Horizon',
        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')

ax.text((x_offsets[0] + x_offsets[1] + cell_w) / 2, -0.45,
        f'Baseline (exp_001): eval = {BASELINE_EVAL:.1f} | '
        'Subsample ON + trained dt_emb → collapse (2/2); '
        'removing dt_emb prevents it',
        ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9, color='#555', style='italic')

outdir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_9/projects/event-gated-adaptive-horizon/artifacts/figures/paper'
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig3_factorial_grid.pdf')
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig3_factorial_grid.png')
plt.close()
print('Saved fig3_factorial_grid.pdf and .png')

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import json
import os
import numpy as np

BASE = '/root/autodl-tmp/event-gated-adaptive-horizon'
LOGDIR = os.path.join(BASE, 'logdir')
FIGDIR = os.path.join(BASE, 'figures')

EXPERIMENTS = {
    'baseline':  ('baseline_s1',                          'Baseline (dt=1)',                    'black',   '-',  2.0),
    '008a':      ('exp_008a_fixed_dt2_no_subsample',      'dt=2, no subsample, dt_emb untrained', '#1f77b4', '-',  1.5),
    '008e_v3':   ('exp_008e_v3_subsample_on_dt1_h15',     'subsample ON, dt_emb untrained, H=15','#2ca02c', '-',  1.5),
    '008f':      ('exp_008f_no_dt_embed_subsample_on_h8', 'subsample ON, dt_emb=0, H=8',        '#9467bd', '-',  1.5),
    '008d':      ('exp_008d_subsample_on_h8',             'subsample ON, dt_emb trained, H=8',  '#d62728', '--', 1.5),
    '006':       ('fixed_dt2_v1_s1',                      'dt=2, subsample ON, dt_emb trained',  '#ff7f0e', '--', 1.5),
    '008c':      ('exp_008c_fixed_dt2_no_subsample_h8',   'no subsample, dt_emb untrained, H=8','#7f7f7f', '-',  1.2),
}

BASELINE_VE = {
    25000: 0.087, 35000: 0.241, 45000: 0.331, 55000: 0.404,
    65000: 0.563, 75000: 0.719, 85000: 0.701, 95000: 0.632, 105000: 0.656,
}

def load_metrics(logdir_name):
    path = os.path.join(LOGDIR, logdir_name, 'metrics.jsonl')
    eval_data = {}
    train_data = {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            row = json.loads(line)
            step = row['step']
            if 'eval_return' in row:
                eval_data[step] = row['eval_return']
            if 'value_mean' in row:
                train_data[step] = row['value_mean']
    return eval_data, train_data

def compute_ve(eval_data, train_data):
    ve = {}
    for step in sorted(eval_data.keys()):
        if step in train_data and eval_data[step] != 0:
            ve[step] = train_data[step] / eval_data[step]
    return ve

all_data = {}
for key, (logdir_name, label, color, ls, lw) in EXPERIMENTS.items():
    eval_d, train_d = load_metrics(logdir_name)
    ve = compute_ve(eval_d, train_d)
    all_data[key] = {'eval': eval_d, 'train': train_d, 've': ve,
                     'label': label, 'color': color, 'ls': ls, 'lw': lw}

# ── Figure 1: Learning Curves ──
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for key in ['baseline', '008a', '008e_v3', '008f', '008d', '006', '008c']:
    d = all_data[key]
    steps = sorted(d['eval'].keys())
    vals = [d['eval'][s] for s in steps]
    ax.plot(np.array(steps)/1000, vals, label=d['label'],
            color=d['color'], linestyle=d['ls'], linewidth=d['lw'])

ax.axhline(y=950, color='black', linestyle=':', linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.6)
ax.annotate('baseline asymptote (~950)', xy=(350, 950), fontsize=9,
            color='black', alpha=0.7, va='bottom')

ax.set_xlabel('Training Step (×1K)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Eval Return', fontsize=12)
ax.set_title('Learning Curves: Eval Return vs Training Step', fontsize=14)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)
ax.legend(fontsize=8.5, loc='lower right', framealpha=0.9)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGDIR, 'fig1_learning_curves.pdf'), dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGDIR, 'fig1_learning_curves.png'), dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close(fig)
print('Figure 1 saved.')

# ── Figure 2: Normalized V/E Ratio ──
baseline_ve_steps = sorted(BASELINE_VE.keys())
baseline_ve_interp = {}
for key in all_data:
    if key == 'baseline':
        continue
    for step in sorted(all_data[key]['ve'].keys()):
        if step not in baseline_ve_interp and step >= baseline_ve_steps[0]:

1	\section{Results}
2	\label{sec:results}
3	
4	We organize results around six findings (F1--F6) that establish a causal chain from trained temporal conditioning to pathological value dynamics and performance collapse. All experiments use Walker Walk (DMC) with DreamerV3; treatments run to 105K steps and the baseline to 505K steps. We report evaluation returns (mean over 10 episodes) and the normalized value-to-eval ratio ($\nve$), defined as the ratio of a configuration's imagined value to evaluation return, normalized by the baseline's ratio at the same training step.
5	
6	%% ============================================================
7	%% TABLE 1: Main results summary
8	%% ============================================================
9	
10	\begin{table*}[t]
11	\centering
12	\caption{All configurations and outcomes. NVE reports peak $\nve$ in the 35K+ window (\S\ref{sec:metrics}). CIVO-positive seeds are shaded; $\dagger$\,marks a false positive (non-CIVO collapse with elevated NVE).}
13	\label{tab:main_results}
14	\footnotesize
15	\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
16	\begin{tabular}{llcccccl}
17	\toprule
18	\textbf{Exp} & \textbf{Config} & \textbf{dt\_emb} & \textbf{Sub} & \textbf{H} & \textbf{Eval@final} & \textbf{NVE} & \textbf{Outcome} \\
19	\midrule
20	001 & Baseline ($\dt{=}1$) & --- & OFF & 15 & 915.7 @105K & 1.00$\times$ & Healthy \\
21	\rowcolor{gray!15}
22	006 & Fixed $\dt{=}2$ & trained & OFF & 15 & 132.9 @65K & 4.83$\times$ & Collapsed \\
23	007 & Fixed $\dt{=}4$ & trained & OFF & 15 & 152.5 @55K & --- & Collapsed \\
24	005 & Learned gate & trained & ON & 15 & 98.8 @145K & --- & Collapsed \\
25	\midrule
26	\rowcolor{gray!15}
27	008d & Factorial (s0) & trained & ON & 8 & 82.8 @55K & 4.12$\times$ & Full collapse \\
28	\rowcolor{gray!15}
29	009b & Factorial (s2) & trained & ON & 8 & 267.9 @105K & 1.62$\times$ & Transient CIVO \\
30	\rowcolor{gray!15}
31	009e & Factorial (s1) & trained & ON & 8 & 131.1 @105K & 4.12$\times$ & Oscillatory \\
32	008f & No dt\_emb (s0) & none & ON & 8 & 503.0 @105K & 0.97$\times$ & Healthy \\
33	009c & No dt\_emb (s2) & none & ON & 8 & 148.3 @105K & 1.14$\times$ & Declining \\
34	008a & No subsample & untrained & OFF & 15 & 777.7 @105K & 0.93$\times$ & Healthy \\
35	008c & No subsample & untrained & OFF & 8 & 240.9 @65K & 0.58$\times$ & Slow learner \\
36	\midrule
37	008e\_v3 s1 & Mitigation & trained & ON & 15 & 869.9 @105K & 0.94$\times$ & Healthy \\
38	008e\_v3 s2$^\dagger$ & Mitigation & trained & ON & 15 & 137.0 @105K & 3.78$\times$ & Non-CIVO collapse \\
39	009a & Baseline (s2) & --- & OFF & 15 & 836.5 @105K & --- & Healthy \\
40	\bottomrule
41	\end{tabular}
42	\end{table*}
43	
44	%% ============================================================
45	%% F1: All dt>1 degrade
46	%% ============================================================
47	
48	\subsection{F1: All Variable-Rate Configurations Degrade}
49	\label{sec:f1}
50	
51	Every configuration that introduces $\dt > 1$ imagination degrades relative to the $\dt{=}1$ baseline, regardless of mechanism (Figure~\ref{fig:learning_curves}). The baseline (exp\_001) reaches 915.7 at 105K steps and peaks at 970.4 at 505K. In contrast, fixed $\dt{=}2$ (exp\_006) peaks at 485.3 at 35K before collapsing to 132.9 by 65K---a $-73\%$ decline from its own peak (14\% of baseline). Fixed $\dt{=}4$ (exp\_007) peaks at only 176.9 at 25K and never exceeds 152.5 thereafter. The learned-gate configuration (exp\_005) peaks at 541.2 at 55K but collapses to 98.8 by 145K. This uniform degradation motivates the factorial analysis that follows.
52	
53	\begin{figure}[t]
54	\centering
55	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_learning_curves.pdf}
56	\caption{Learning curves for all configurations. The $\dt{=}1$ baseline (black) reaches 915.7 at 105K; all variable-rate configurations degrade, with fixed $\dt{=}4$ and the learned gate collapsing most severely.}
57	\label{fig:learning_curves}
58	\end{figure}
59	
60	%% ============================================================
61	%% F2: Trained dt_embedding → nve > 1.5x
62	%% ============================================================
63	
64	\subsection{F2: Trained Temporal Embedding Triggers Value Overestimation}
65	\label{sec:f2}
66	
67	The factorial design isolates trained $\dt$-embedding as the factor that reliably triggers pathological value overestimation. The key causal control compares exp\_008d (trained $\dt$-embedding, subsampling ON, $H{=}8$) against exp\_008f (identical configuration but \emph{no} trained $\dt$-embedding). As shown in Figure~\ref{fig:nve_trajectory}:
68	
69	\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
70	\item \textbf{008d} (trained): $\nve = 1.78\times$ at 25K $\rightarrow$ $4.12\times$ at 55K $\rightarrow$ collapse (eval 167$\rightarrow$82.8).
71	\item \textbf{008f} (no dt\_emb): $\nve = 1.02\times$ at 25K $\rightarrow$ $0.30\times$ at 105K $\rightarrow$ no collapse (eval 503.0 at 105K).
72	\end{itemize}
73	
74	In the 35K+ window (\S\ref{sec:metrics}), the $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ threshold correctly classifies 7/8 seeds (AUROC${=}0.933$, Clopper--Pearson 95\% CI $[0.47, 1.0]$): 3 CIVO-positive (exp\_006, 008d, 009b) and 4 CIVO-negative, with one non-CIVO false positive (008e\_v3 s2, $3.78\times$; \S\ref{sec:f6}).  The gap between the lowest true positive ($1.62\times$) and the highest true negative ($1.00\times$) is $0.62$.
75	
76	\begin{figure}[t]
77	\centering
78	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig2_nve_trajectory.pdf}
79	\caption{Normalized value-to-eval ratio ($\nve$) trajectories. The dashed line marks the $1.5\times$ threshold. All trained-embedding configurations with $\dt > 1$ imagination (red/orange) exceed this threshold; the mitigation configuration (008e\_v3 s1, dash-dot) with $\dt{=}1$-only imagination remains below it.}
80	\label{fig:nve_trajectory}
81	\end{figure}
82	
83	\paragraph{Three post-CIVO outcomes.}
84	Running the 008d configuration with two independent seeds (s0, s2) and an extended replication of seed 1 (009e, continuing the same training run) reveals that trained $\dt$-embedding triggers CIVO---yet the downstream consequence is stochastic:
85	
86	%% ============================================================
87	%% TABLE 3: Three post-CIVO outcomes
88	%% ============================================================
89	
90	\begin{table}[t]
91	\centering
92	\caption{Post-CIVO outcomes for the 008d configuration. Peak/Final NVE measured in the 35K+ window. Seeds 0 and 2 are independent runs; seed 1 (009e) is an extended replication.}
93	\label{tab:post_civo}
94	\footnotesize
95	\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
96	\begin{tabular}{lcccl}
97	\toprule
98	\textbf{Seed} & \textbf{Peak} & \textbf{Final} & \textbf{Eval} & \textbf{Outcome} \\
99	\midrule
100	s0 (008d) & 4.12$\times$ & 4.12$\times$ & 82.8 & Full collapse \\
101	s2 (009b) & 1.62$\times$ & 0.38$\times$ & 267.9 & Transient CIVO \\
102	s1 (009e) & 4.12$\times$ & 1.57$\times$ & 131.1 & Oscillatory \\
103	\bottomrule
104	\end{tabular}
105	\end{table}
106	
107	\noindent\textbf{Seed 0 (008d):} Full collapse (Pathway A). Value explosion ($+130\%$), evaluation declines from 167 to 82.8, entropy decreases---the classic CIVO feedback loop.
108	
109	\noindent\textbf{Seed 2 (009b):} Transient CIVO. The $\nve$ reaches $1.62\times$ at 45K (35K+ window), exceeding the $1.5\times$ threshold, but the value function self-corrects to $0.38\times$ by 105K, and evaluation recovers to 267.9. This demonstrates the threshold's sensitivity to early CIVO signals even in cases that spontaneously recover.
110	
111	\noindent\textbf{Seed 1 (009e):} Oscillatory degradation. Evaluation oscillates between 82.7 and 250 before settling at 131.1; the value function rises then reverses (peak $\nve = 4.12\times$ at 55K, final $1.57\times$).
112	
113	All runs exceed $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ in the 35K+ window, confirming deterministic CIVO triggering, but downstream outcomes are seed-dependent (1/2 persistent collapse rate among independent seeds).
114	
115	%% ============================================================
116	%% F3: Untrained dt_embedding prevents drift
117	%% ============================================================
118	
119	\subsection{F3: Untrained Temporal Embedding Prevents Drift}
120	\label{sec:f3}
121	
122	\begin{figure}[t]
123	\centering
124	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig3_factorial_grid.pdf}
125	\caption{Factorial experiment summary. Each cell shows final evaluation return and $\nve$ status. Trained $\dt$-embedding is the sole factor that separates collapsed (red) from healthy (green) configurations.}
126	\label{fig:factorial_grid}
127	\end{figure}
128	
129	When the $\dt$-embedding is present but \emph{untrained} (fixed random projection), value dynamics remain healthy: exp\_008a reaches 777.7 ($\nve = 0.59\times$) and exp\_008c reaches 240.9 ($\nve = 0.58\times$), with no pathological overestimation.  This identifies \emph{training} of the temporal embedding---not its architectural presence---as the causal factor: the untrained embedding provides a temporal signal without co-adapting with the reward head.
130	
131	%% ============================================================
132	%% F4: dt=2 > dt=4 monotonic degradation
133	%% ============================================================
134	
135	\subsection{F4: Degradation Scales Monotonically with \texorpdfstring{$\dt$}{dt}}
136	\label{sec:f4}
137	
138	\begin{figure}[t]
139	\centering
140	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig5_dt_amplification.pdf}
141	\caption{Peak evaluation return as a function of imagination $\dt$. Performance degrades monotonically: $\dt{=}1$ (915.7) $>$ $\dt{=}2$ (485.3, $-47\%$) $>$ $\dt{=}4$ (176.9, $-81\%$).}
142	\label{fig:dt_amplification}
143	\end{figure}
144	
145	The magnitude of degradation scales monotonically with the imagination step size (Figure~\ref{fig:dt_amplification}). From the $\dt{=}1$ baseline (915.7 at 105K), fixed $\dt{=}2$ (exp\_006) achieves a peak of only 485.3 ($-47\%$), and fixed $\dt{=}4$ (exp\_007) peaks at 176.9 ($-81\%$). This monotonic relationship is consistent with compounding model error: larger temporal gaps amplify the RSSM's prediction inaccuracy at each imagination step, and these errors accumulate across the rollout horizon.
146	
147	%% ============================================================
148	%% F5: Horizon and subsample secondary
149	%% ============================================================
150	
151	\subsection{F5: Imagination Horizon and Subsampling Are Secondary Factors}
152	\label{sec:f5}
153	
154	Neither horizon length nor temporal subsampling triggers collapse without a trained $\dt$-embedding: both untrained configurations maintain $\nve < 0.6\times$ (\S\ref{sec:f3}), while the trained counterpart (008d) collapses with $\nve = 4.12\times$.  The no-embedding configurations show cross-seed variance (008f: 503.0 vs.\ 009c: 148.3) but neither exhibits $\nve > 1.5\times$---confirming that low evaluation alone does not indicate CIVO.
155	
156	%% ============================================================
157	%% F6: dt=1 imagination does not prevent collapse
158	%% ============================================================
159	
160	\subsection{F6: Restricting Imagination to \texorpdfstring{$\dt{=}1$}{dt=1} Does Not Prevent Collapse}
161	\label{sec:f6}
162	
163	\begin{figure}[t]
164	\centering
165	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig6_multiple_pathways.pdf}
166	\caption{Contrasting collapse dynamics. \textbf{Left:} 008d (classic CIVO)---value explosion precedes evaluation decline, entropy decreases. \textbf{Right:} 008e\_v3 seed 2 (non-CIVO)---evaluation crashes while value remains stable, entropy \emph{increases}. Baseline seed 2 (009a, dashed) remains stable at 836.5, ruling out seed fragility.}
167	\label{fig:multiple_pathways}
168	\end{figure}
169	
170	The mitigation experiment exp\_008e\_v3 restricts imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained $\dt$-embedding for observation conditioning. If CIVO were the sole vulnerability pathway, this restriction should prevent collapse. Results are mixed:
171	
172	\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
173	\item \textbf{Seed 1} (008e\_v3\_s1): Healthy. Eval 869.9 at 105K ($95\%$ of baseline), $\nve = 0.80\times$.
174	\item \textbf{Seed 2} (008e\_v3\_s2): Collapsed. Eval drops from 715 to 137 at 105K, $\nve = 3.78\times$.
175	\end{itemize}
176	
177	The baseline with seed 2 (exp\_009a) is stable at 836.5 at 105K, ruling out inherent seed fragility as the explanation.
178	
179	\paragraph{Distinct collapse mechanisms.}
180	The collapse dynamics of 008e\_v3\_s2 differ qualitatively from the classic CIVO observed in 008d (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}, Figure~\ref{fig:multiple_pathways}):
181	
182	\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
183	\item \textbf{008d (CIVO, Pathway A):} value explosion ($+130\%$) $\rightarrow$ evaluation decline $\rightarrow$ entropy decreases.
184	\item \textbf{008e\_v3\_s2 (non-CIVO, Pathway B):} evaluation crashes ($-81\%$) $\rightarrow$ value remains stable $\rightarrow$ entropy \emph{increases} ($-5.21 \rightarrow -3.83$).
185	\end{itemize}
186	
187	In Pathway A, the critic drives collapse through systematic overestimation; in Pathway B, the actor destabilizes independently while the critic remains initially well-calibrated. Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ prevents the CIVO mechanism---no early $\nve$ spike, no reward amplification---but seed-dependent late-stage policy instability (Pathway B) can still occur.
188	
189	This case also produces the sole false positive in the $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ classification: 008e\_v3\_s2's late evaluation decline inflates $\nve$ to $3.78\times$ through a non-CIVO mechanism (\S\ref{sec:pathways}).
190	
191	%% ============================================================
192	%% TABLE 2: RSSM Fidelity
193	%% ============================================================
194	
195	\begin{table}[t]
196	\centering
197	\caption{RSSM fidelity at $\dt{=}1$ vs.\ $\dt{=}2$. Trained embedding (008d) produces $2.78\times$ reward gap; removing it (008f) eliminates the gap but degrades absolute prediction.}
198	\label{tab:rssm_fidelity}
199	\footnotesize
200	\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
201	\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
202	\toprule
203	& \multicolumn{3}{c}{\textbf{obs\_MSE}} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{\textbf{reward\_MAE}} \\
204	\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-7}
205	\textbf{Config} & $\dt{=}1$ & $\dt{=}2$ & Gap & $\dt{=}1$ & $\dt{=}2$ & Gap \\
206	\midrule
207	Baseline & 13.49 & 27.50 & 2.04$\times$ & 0.0102 & 0.0159 & 1.56$\times$ \\
208	008d (trained) & 41.31 & 53.67 & 1.30$\times$ & 0.0568 & 0.1579 & 2.78$\times$ \\
209	008f (no emb) & 8.01 & 22.04 & 2.75$\times$ & 0.7469 & 0.7526 & 1.01$\times$ \\
210	\bottomrule
211	\end{tabular}
212	\end{table}
213	
214	\paragraph{RSSM fidelity analysis.}
215	Table~\ref{tab:rssm_fidelity} reveals the mechanism underlying CIVO. The trained $\dt$-embedding in 008d produces a $2.78\times$ gap in reward prediction error between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$ trajectories. This asymmetric fidelity means the reward head systematically overpredicts rewards at $\dt{=}2$, which the critic internalizes as optimistic value estimates. In contrast, 008f (no embedding) shows a $1.01\times$ gap---the reward head cannot distinguish temporal scales, which eliminates the exploitation channel but at the cost of severely degraded absolute reward prediction ($0.7469$ MAE vs.\ $0.0568$ for 008d at $\dt{=}1$).
216	
217	\paragraph{Summary.}
218	F1--F5 establish trained $\dt$-embedding as the causal factor (7/8 classification, one non-CIVO false positive), with degradation scaling monotonically with $\dt$.  F6 shows that restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ prevents CIVO but not all collapse modes: $\nve$ is a sensitive but non-specific warning indicator requiring joint analysis with collapse signatures for mechanistic attribution.
